Faithfulness Report (pladdrr vs Praat)

Source: vignettes/agents/faithfulness-report.Rmd
faithfulness-report.Rmd

Generated: 2026-11-09 21:00:18 CET

Each row is one Praat DSP routine. Praat output is the oracle; pladdrr is checked against it at the documented tolerance. pass = within tolerance, fail = drift (open an issue or document the rationale).

A routine with several values shows its first value; |Δ| is the largest over all of them (n = number of values).

Routine Status n Praat pladdrr Δ

Sound -> Intensity -> mean (dB) pass 1 84.94803 84.94803 3.075786e-07 1e-06

Non-determinism caveat (CPPS row above): the tolerance reported for CPPS (calculate_cpps_ultra) reflects the deterministic fast/default trend-fit path (fit_method = "robust", Siegel). Praat’s own fit_method = "robust slow" (Theil-Sen) trend fit is not deterministic — a documented upstream Praat defect — and samples randomly: ~0.8 dB spread across identical runs of the same input, with occasional extreme outliers around 1e290. pladdrr reproduces that non-determinism faithfully when "robust slow" is requested (see agent-guide.Rmd v4.9.19 entry and praat-modifications.Rmd v4.9.19). Do not read the row above as evidence that the robust-slow path is bit-reproducible — it is not, in Praat or in pladdrr.

Oracle version (CPPS row above): the CPPS row agrees with Praat 6.4.47 to 0.003 dB. Against Praat 6.4.27 the same pipeline differs by about +0.13 dB: Praat rewrote its CPP-to-CPPS post-processing between those releases (max(raw) - trend became max(raw - trend), and the robust trend estimator changed), so a gap of that size against an older oracle is a version difference, not a pladdrr defect. Say which Praat produced a reference number.

Oracle version (FormantPath rows): the 2026-11 external review ran this registry against Praat 6.4.27 and found the mean F1 / F2 rows off by 0.138 Hz / 0.0256 Hz, with identical frame count and step; it attributed that to the candidate-grid origin (0 in 6.4.27, 0.0275 s in the 6.4.47 code vendored here). Those figures were not reproduced against 6.4.27 here; against 6.4.47 the rows pass. Treat a gap of that size against an older oracle as a version difference, and do not widen the tolerance for it: the same tolerance guards real drift.

MFCC rows: Praat’s To MFCC takes (first filter, distance, max) where Sound$to_mfcc() takes (f1_mel, fmax_mel, df_mel). The frame-count row passed while the two were crossed, so the coefficient row exists to catch a wrong mapping; against 6.4.47 the coefficients agree to about 2.5e-10.

Platform caveat (Intensity row above): on Apple Silicon the reference Praat application and pladdrr can differ by ~2e-6 dB in an energy-averaged Intensity mean at the default time step (measured against Praat 6.4.47 with byte-identical input: 87.415718735 vs 87.415720871; every other step size tried agrees to all printed digits, and the 2026-11 audit found Linux x86-64 agreeing against Praat 6.4.27). Frame centres x1 + (i-1)*dx land exactly on a rounding boundary of Sampled_xToNearestIndex for the default grid, and a fused multiply-add changes the chosen centre sample in 5 of the 117 frames (reproduced with math.fma). pladdrr disables floating-point contraction on purpose (#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF in melder.h), so it follows the non-fused result. That the app is built with contraction is inferred from the simulation, not from its build flags. Treat differences of this size on a frame grid that hits exact sample boundaries as a platform artifact, not a pladdrr defect; the 1e-05 tolerance above already covers it.

Oracle: Praat 6.4.47 (November 7 2025) on Darwin (aarch64-apple-darwin23).
